uncited: AMR-KDTree Leaf Filtering is a traversal optimization for Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) volume rendering that accelerates isosurface extraction by pruning leaf nodes of an AMR-KDTree based on scalar value ranges.

It builds on [Min/Max Tree Construction](1623-min-max-tree-construction.md) but applies the filtering specifically to the leaf nodes of the AMR-KDTree structure, which represent regions of uniform brick origin.

Unlike sibling methods that may filter at coarser levels or use complex bounding volumes, this method leverages the pre-computed min/max values of the finest-level cells within each leaf to immediately discard regions that do not contain the target isovalue, reducing redundant octant generation and vertex computation.
Pointers to coarser bricks overlapping the leaf's region.
The minimum ($v_{min}$) and maximum ($v_{max}$) scalar values of all cells in the finest-level brick within that leaf.
- A set of active octants (or dual cells) derived only from leaf nodes where $v_{min} \le I \le v_{max}$.
**Tree Construction:** Build the AMR-KDTree over the AMR dataset.
For each leaf node, identify the finest-level brick covering its region.
**Traversal:** Perform a traversal of the AMR-KDTree.
**Pruning:** If the condition is false, ignore (prune) this leaf node and do not process its cells.
- **Brick Overlap:** A single brick may be listed in multiple leaves.
A data structure introduced by Wald et al. [38] for efficient access to AMR cells, built over external memory with little memory or compute overhead.
It serves as the foundation for AMR-KDTree Leaf Filtering.
Leaf nodes represent regions where all cells come from the same brick, storing pointers to the finest-level brick, coarser overlapping bricks, and the value range of finest-level cells.
- **Time Complexity:** Filtering is $O(1)$ per leaf node, as it involves a simple range check.
The overall traversal time is proportional to the number of leaves, but the number of leaves processed for octant generation is reduced by the filtering step.
- **Performance:** Significantly reduces redundant computation by avoiding octant generation for leaves that do not contain the isovalue.
- **Limitations:** Filtering is only applied at the leaf level; coarser levels do not benefit from this specific optimization.
Requires pre-computation of value ranges for all leaves.
The AMR-KDTree was introduced by Wald et al. [38] for efficient access to AMR cells.
The method addresses the problem of redundant computation in octant generation by leveraging value range information stored in the AMR-KDTree leaves.
